summary: Asteroid mining is a long-term real economic opportunity enabled by Starship reusability, with Psyche asteroid containing more precious metals than Earth's entire crust
summary_extended: Baker argues that asteroid mining — specifically the capture of the Psyche asteroid, which he claims contains more precious metals than exist in Earth's entire crust — represents a genuine long-term economic opportunity enabled by SpaceX's Starship reusability. He describes a scenario in which Psyche is maneuvered into a stable geosynchronous orbit above a US-controlled Pacific atoll, with Tesla Optimus robots performing the physical extraction and materials delivered to Earth via controlled atmospheric re-entry. Baker frames this within Jeff Bezos's broader vision of Earth being 'zoned residential' with all heavy industry relocated to space, positioning asteroid mining as the most economically significant long-term application of SpaceX's launch infrastructure. He prefaces the thesis with 'this sounds crazy' but expresses genuine conviction that 'it's going to be a very real thing,' making this a speculative but sincerely held long-term structural view with no near-term investment implication for publicly traded equities.
detail: Baker describes capturing asteroid Psyche (gold, silver, platinum, all precious metals exceeding Earth's crust), bringing it to stable geosynchronous orbit over a US-controlled Pacific atoll, and using Optimus robots for extraction. Delivery to Earth via controlled re-entry. Jeff Bezos's vision of Earth 'zoned residential' with all heavy industry in space is the long-term frame. Baker calls this 'probably the most futuristic' economic application of SpaceX.
